name: dwdiff
desc: Diff that operates at the word level
why: A word-level diff is a genuinely different way to see changes in prose, though it is a niche variant of a familiar idea.

brief.what_it_is: dwdiff is a command-line diff program that compares text word by word rather than line by line. It takes two text inputs and prints the new text with deleted and inserted words marked up, and command-line options change what is printed and which markers are used. Users can set which characters count as whitespace, and can supply a list of delimiter characters that are treated as words even when no whitespace separates them from neighbouring text. It ships with a companion program, dwfilter. The page says it is mostly command-line compatible with wdiff.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation beyond offering a word-level alternative to line-based diff. Its stated differences from wdiff are configurable whitespace and optional delimiter characters.
brief.how_it_works: The page describes the default output as the new text with deleted and inserted parts annotated with markers. Delimiters are single characters treated as words even when no whitespace separates them from preceding words or delimiters. The page does not describe the internal algorithm.
brief.install_notes: The page lists packages from several distributions and platforms: Fedora Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, Mac OS X via MacPorts or Homebrew, Slackware via Slackbuilds.org and Slacky.eu, Solaris via sunfreeware.com, and OpenPKG. Otherwise it can be built from source. The 2.1.2 release note mentions use of ICU and a switch from icu-config to pkg-config, which suggests ICU and pkg-config are build dependencies, but the page does not spell out build steps. No accounts or runtime configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: Its delimiter concept lets punctuation such as commas or dashes count as standalone tokens even when attached to words, which matters for prose diffs where plain whitespace splitting blurs changes. Configurable whitespace and delimiters are the stated distinction from wdiff.
brief.status: Quiet. The most recent release listed is version 2.1.4 on 13-Dec-2020, and the page was last modified on 2020-12-13. Earlier releases are 2.1.3 (18-Jul-2020) and 2.1.2 (10-Dec-2018). The site footer reads copyright 2005-2025, so the site itself is still up. The homepage shows no releases from 2021 onward, and I did not check a repository for commit activity.
brief.caveats: The page says --autopager, --terminal and --avoid-wraps are not supported, so it is not a full drop-in for wdiff. It is distributed under GPL version 3; versions before 1.3 were under the Open Software License 2.0. The last release is from 2020. The source download link is labelled 'here' but its target URL was not captured, so I did not confirm the repository location. The homepage is the only page I read.
quotes: dwdiff is a diff program that operates at the word level instead of the line level.
Delimiters are single characters that are treated as if they are words, even when there is no whitespace separating them from preceding words or delimiters.
The default output from dwdiff is the new text, with the deleted and inserted parts annotated with markers.
